title: "Sita Aaj Lanka Khud Jalane Aayi Hai": The Alpha Trailer Hands the YRF Spy Universe to Two Women — and a Hrithik Cameo Lit the Fuse
excerpt: Alia Bhatt and Sharvari throw the first all-female punch in Aditya Chopra's spy empire. The trailer is loud, divisive, and ends on a crossover tease that broke the internet. In cinemas July 3.
body:
The trailer opens on a little girl learning to kill. By the time it ends ninety seconds later, **Alia Bhatt** is walking through fire in a backless combat fit, looking straight down the lens, and delivering the line that has already been screenshotted into oblivion: *"Sita aaj Lanka khud jalane aayi hai."* Sita has come to burn down Lanka herself. The YRF Spy Universe has never sounded like this — because it has never been a woman's voice before.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=QRqGwGwo1Y0</youtube>

**Alpha**, the newest chapter in Aditya Chopra's billion-rupee spy machine, dropped its full trailer this week, and Yash Raj announced it with a caption that tells you exactly the register they're going for: *"girls just want to have fun…with guns."* This is the franchise that gave us Tiger, Pathaan, and War — all chiselled men in slow motion — finally handing the keys to two women and daring the audience to keep up.


> "Welcome to the newest chapter of the YRF Spy Universe — an edgy origin story of a girl raised and built to kill." — Yash Raj Films

The setup is pure pulp, and it works. Alia plays Sita, a girl meticulously groomed from childhood by a father figure — a quietly menacing **Bobby Deol** — and engineered into the perfect weapon for a shadowy programme called Alpha. Then she learns what the programme actually is, and she goes rogue against the very system that built her. Enter **Sharvari**, who detonates into the back half of the trailer looking fierce and genuinely dangerous, matching Alia punch for punch. The hand-to-hand sequences between the two leads are the trailer's best argument for itself: raw, close, unglamorous in the way good action is, and refreshingly free of a man stepping in to finish the fight.

**Anil Kapoor** lurks in the margins, all silver-fox gravitas, presumably as the franchise's institutional spine. But the moment that actually broke the timeline arrives right at the end — a blink-and-you-miss-it crossover tease, with **Hrithik Roshan** (reportedly reprising Kabir from *War*) surfacing to cement Alpha's place in the larger Spyverse. The internet did the rest. That single frame did more for the film's trending numbers than the entire rest of the cut.

Not that the reception has been uniformly adoring. Let's be honest about the noise. A vocal section of the fandom has spent the week unconvinced — some calling the teaser a *La Femme Nikita* tribute act, others grumbling that Alia, coming off the box-office stumble of *Jigra*, is a risky bet to shoulder a tentpole this size. There's a real debate about whether the trailer gave away too much plot. It's the kind of pre-release pile-on that either evaporates on opening Friday or curdles into a problem. The honest read: the marketing has been uneven, but the central image — two women running a spy franchise built entirely on male swagger — is the most interesting thing YRF has tried in years.

The pedigree backs the ambition. **Shiv Rawail**, who made the quietly devastating *The Railway Men*, directs. The story comes from Uday Chopra, screenplay by Shridhar Raghavan (the man who architected *War*), dialogue by Ishita Moitra, and that crunching action design from Craig Macrae and Sunil Rodrigues. The DNA is unmistakably Spyverse — but pointed somewhere new.

For the diaspora, **Alpha** releases in cinemas worldwide on **July 3, 2026**, going head-to-head with Huma Qureshi's *Baby Do Die Do* the same day. Expect wide theatrical runs across the US, UK, Canada, and the Gulf through YRF's international network — this is a banner that takes its overseas Friday very seriously, and a Hrithik cameo only sweetens the NRI multiplex pull. A streaming home will follow, almost certainly on Amazon Prime Video, where YRF has parked its recent slate, though no OTT date has been confirmed.

Whether Alpha lands as a genuine reinvention or an expensive swing-and-a-miss, one thing is already settled: the most talked-about action hero of this YRF summer is a woman who just announced, on the record, that she's come to burn the whole thing down. We'll find out on July 3 whether the box office lets her strike the match.
